title: Folate (Vitamin B9)
attribution: Source: MedlinePlus, National Library of Medicine.
measures: Folate, also called vitamin B9, helps the body make healthy new cells. It is often measured together with vitamin B12, particularly when investigating certain types of anemia.
low: A folate deficiency can contribute to anemia. Possible causes of a B vitamin deficiency include celiac disease, Crohn's disease, alcohol use disorder, malabsorption, digestive surgery, certain medicines and some gene changes such as in the MTHFR gene.
high: MedlinePlus notes that large amounts of B vitamins can cause health problems.
notes: Deficiencies are less common in the United States because many foods are fortified. Laboratories use different reference ranges, and inflammation and some medicines can affect results.
